newsitem.title: UK: Euro products outlook - supply may give bumpy ride.
newsitem.headline: Euro products outlook - supply may give bumpy ride.

text.p: Most European oil products could be hard pressured to maintain value this week in the face of a looser supply/demand balance, traders said.

High and low sulphur fuel oil cargo prices are unlikely to rise far this week amid continued good offers of low sulphur cracked cargoes as well as Russian high sulphur straight-run cargoes, traders said.

Business on Thursday and Friday took some of the obvious length out of northwest Europe's low sulphur market. But cargoes remain in overhang in the region and in the absence of fresh Italian buying, prices will languish.
In contrast to previous winters, Russian cargoes continue to flow out of the Baltic. One regular buyer said he saw five, most of which were of E-4 quality, loading in the next ten days.
Although supply of high sulphur barrels for the next couple of weeks are limited, utility demand is mostly covered and is unlikely to provide much support.
Naphtha may have a bumpy ride and prices could come under pressure unless more end-user demand kicks in.
End-users have been relaxed since the New Year, with most having covered their short-term requirement ahead of the Christmas break.

If, as some dealers maintain, end-user demand does not significantly revive until mid February naphtha could slip below $220 cif NWE this week. But if end-users continue to pick up bits and pieces, demand should maintain prices.

Gasoline will still look to the U.S for direction this week in order to draw off some European supplies which are set to remain high given that local refineries are pumping out mogas in order to meet middle distillates demand.
"If the U.S doesn't gain Europe will have to shed some weight and start moving material out of the region," said one trader.
Prices for Eurograde may slip to the mid $200 teens cif NWE or a touch lower to open the arb. However, if the U.S strengthens, European prices will be supported or even boosted.

Traders cranking up February programmes could enliven gas oil business after a lethargic week dampened variously by normal temperatures, ice-related transport problems and a demand lull that followed heavy buying during the New Year freeze.

In barges, a thaw that has eased supply bottlenecks and milder than expected temperatures could shave $1 or $1.50 off heating oil and low sulphur diesel premiums to around Feb IPE +$3 and +$11 respectively.
"As long as we don't see frost or snow inland we won't have a demand spike. There is plenty of product around (in ARA)," a trader said.
Cargo traders see some tightness in low sulphur diesel continuing to put a floor under premiums at Feb IPE +$18/20, with continuing French and German interest leading the market.

Heating oil demand could lift premiums as buying for February kicks in, but ample Russian supply from the Baltic could help depress premiums for early month Russian to around Feb IPE +$3.50 and for French grade to around Feb IPE +$8.
